trigger: Waterborne emergency, such as a failure or significant interruption in key water treatment processes (for example unsafe chemical feed or loss of treatment affecting water that reached distribution), or another situation the primacy agency designates Tier 1
deadline: As soon as practical but no later than 24 hours after the system learns of the situation
notify: All persons served by the affected system, by broadcast media, posting, hand delivery, or another method approved in writing by the primacy agency
applies_at_this_tier: Yes for each affected water system if key treatment was interrupted or off-spec water may have entered distribution
notifying_entity: Water Utility (VP of Water Quality and Compliance for each affected system)
clock_starts: When the water system learns of the situation

trigger: Same as the Tier 1 notice
deadline: Initiate as soon as practical but no later than 24 hours after the system learns of the situation; then follow any added requirements from the consultation
notify: State drinking water primacy agency of each affected system (after-hours contacts in each PN SOP)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes with any Tier 1 situation. Company rule: also call for any confirmed tampering, even without a Tier 1 trigger
notifying_entity: Water Utility (VP of Water Quality and Compliance for each affected system)
clock_starts: When the water system learns of the situation

obligation: Report failure to comply with a drinking water regulation
trigger: The incident causes a violation of a national primary drinking water regulation, including missed required monitoring
deadline: Within 48 hours (unless the part sets a different period)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if a violation results (for example missed compliance monitoring while SCADA is down)
notifying_entity: Water Utility (VP of Water Quality and Compliance for each affected system)
clock_starts: When the failure to comply occurs or is known

trigger: Completion of the initial public notice and any repeat notices
deadline: Within 10 days of completing the public notification requirements, with a representative copy of each type of notice
applies_at_this_tier: Yes after any public notice
notifying_entity: Water Utility (VP of Water Quality and Compliance for each affected system)

trigger: Any public notice issued
deadline: Keep copies for 3 years after issuance
applies_at_this_tier: Yes after any public notice
notifying_entity: Water Utility (VP of Water Quality and Compliance for each affected system)

citation: 42 U.S.C. 300i-1 (tampering with a public water system, defined in 300i-1(d) as introducing a contaminant or otherwise interfering with operation with the intention of harming persons, is a federal crime)
trigger: Evidence of tampering or attempted tampering, including an unauthorized control action on SCADA
deadline: No statutory reporting deadline. Company rule: notify the FBI within 1 hour of declaring an OT compromise
notify: FBI field office (and IC3 online report)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes for any confirmed unauthorized control action. Preserve evidence for investigators

citation: Voluntary. No federal mandatory cyber incident reporting rule applied to water systems as of 2026-09-25
trigger: Any significant cyber incident
deadline: As soon as possible. Company rule: within 24 hours of declaration
notify: CISA; the water sector information sharing and analysis center
applies_at_this_tier: Yes (voluntary). Reporting to law enforcement or CISA is also a mitigating factor for OFAC if a ransom is ever considered

citation: Each state's public utility commission rules (generic; not verified in this sample)
trigger: Service interruption or security incident as defined by each state's commission rules
deadline: Per each state's rules (confirm before use)
notify: State utility commission of each affected state
applies_at_this_tier: Check for each of the 6 states; the Water Utility regulatory affairs team keeps the list

obligation: DoD cyber incident report (covered defense information)
trigger: Discovery of a cyber incident affecting a covered contractor information system or the covered defense information in it (any system holding it, including SYS-C1 workspaces or laptops while CUI is there)
deadline: Rapidly report: within 72 hours of discovery. Review for evidence of compromise of covered defense information, including other systems accessed
notify: DoD at https://dibnet.dod.mil (DoD-approved medium assurance certificate required)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if the attacker reached any system holding covered defense information (in this scenario, SYS-C1 workspaces)

trigger: Malicious software discovered and isolated in connection with a reported cyber incident
deadline: With the report process, per DC3 or contracting officer instructions; do not send it to the contracting officer
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if malware is isolated

trigger: Reported cyber incident
deadline: Preserve images of affected systems and relevant monitoring and packet capture data for at least 90 days from the report
applies_at_this_tier: Yes with any DFARS report

obligation: Incident report number to the prime contractor
trigger: Construction reports a cyber incident on a DoD subcontract
deadline: As soon as practicable after reporting to DoD
applies_at_this_tier: Yes for the DoD contracts where Construction is a subcontractor

obligation: Covered telecommunications equipment or services discovered
citation: FAR 52.204-25(d) (Section 889); FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: Contractor identifies covered telecommunications equipment or services in use or delivered
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification (further report within 10 business days). Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
applies_at_this_tier: Yes for Construction and Environmental Services federal contracts if such equipment is found (not part of this scenario)

citation: FAR 52.204-23(c); FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: Contractor identifies a covered article (Kaspersky Lab hardware, software, or services) in use or delivered
deadline: Within 3 business days of identification (further report within 10 business days). Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
applies_at_this_tier: Yes for Construction and Environmental Services federal contracts if a covered article is found (not part of this scenario)

obligation: Supplier notice to the asset owner (intercompany)
citation: Intercompany construction contract security schedule (being added, POAM-019); POL-01 4.8
trigger: Construction learns that its staff, accounts, or laptops may have been used to reach Water Utility OT
deadline: Company rule until the schedule is signed: immediately, on the incident bridge
notify: RS-1 Director of Operations and the Water Utility security and compliance lead

obligation: Client notice of service impact or data exposure

citation: FAR 52.204-21 (no incident reporting paragraph); individual contract terms
trigger: An incident affects FCI or performance at a federal site

notify: Contracting officer where a contract requires it
applies_at_this_tier: Check the 31 federal sites' contracts; FCI was not affected in this scenario

trigger: Registrant determines a cybersecurity incident is material
deadline: 4 business days after the materiality determination (delay possible only on U.S. Attorney General finding)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - the group is an SEC registrant. Severity 1 incidents go to the disclosure committee within 24 hours of declaration (POL-03 4.7)

trigger: Annual report
deadline: With the annual report on Form 10-K
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - describe the incident's effect on the risk management and governance description where relevant

citation: State breach notification statutes (all 50 states, DC, PR, USVI; Guam 9 GCA Ch. 48)
trigger: Breach of computerized personal information of state residents (definitions vary by state)
deadline: Varies by state (for example 'without unreasonable delay' or a fixed number of days)
notify: Affected residents; state attorney general or regulator where the state requires it; consumer reporting agencies above state-set counts
applies_at_this_tier: Only if personal information was accessed (customer data in SYS-W2, employee data). Apply the law of each state where affected individuals reside; Florida rows below are the worked example
notifying_entity: Group Chief Privacy Officer with counsel

trigger: Breach of security of personal information of Florida residents
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe a breach occurred (a 15-day extension for good cause applies only to this notice)
applies_at_this_tier: Only if personal information was accessed; not triggered in this scenario unless analysis shows otherwise

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe a breach occurred
applies_at_this_tier: Only if 500 or more Floridians' personal information was accessed

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at a single time
deadline: Without unreasonable delay
applies_at_this_tier: Only if more than 1,000 individuals are notified

obligation: Third-party agent breach notice to the group (inbound)
trigger: A vendor that maintains or processes personal information for the group (for example the CIS vendor) has a breach
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 10 days after the vendor's determination
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - track in vendor contracts

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: Considering a ransomware payment
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if sanctioned party); law enforcement (FBI) or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: All U.S. persons. Strict liability for payments to sanctioned parties. Applies if the incident turns into extortion

trigger: Covered cyber incident (reasonable belief) or ransom payment

applies_at_this_tier: No - final rule not published as of 2026-09-25. If finalized as proposed, the group would be covered (above the SBA size standard; community water systems serving more than 3,300). Recheck when final

trigger: Suspected security incident
deadline: Per policy (as soon as practicable; call the carrier's breach hotline before hiring outside vendors)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual, not legal
